solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drunken snob with no taste devours a simple meal

indicators.note: something that devours takes another thing inside it, so the shuffled letters swallow the single letter a
a drunken person staggers about, so the letters of the words snob and no taste are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tasteless, inebriated snob wolfing down a humble supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' shuffles SNOB and NO TASTE into BENSONTOAST; 'devours' puts A inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked beans on toast is a classic cheap and plain British supper, a very basic dish.

clue.text: Provide funds for hunting in retreat

parts.note: to back a venture is to finance it
tracking an animal is following its trail when hunting it

explanation.surface: Someone bankrolls a hunt, but the hunting goes into reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back along a route already taken is withdrawing, so the word describes a retreating party.

clue.text: Some scared lads up a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
some of the words means a run of their letters is taken, here across the two words

explanation.surface: A few frightened boys have climbed a tree to escape something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes REDLA from scaRED LAds; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: After the last of chips are almost finished, eat fish

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here the end of chips
the word are is not quite completed, losing its final letter

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Once the chips are nearly gone, someone tucks into the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' reads as an order instruction but is only surface; the pieces simply run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: The sardine is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Planes flying somewhere in Italy

indicators.note: aircraft flying about move around, so the letters of the word planes are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aircraft heading to an Italian destination.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is a major southern Italian port, the capital of Campania.

clue.text: Writer entering big public competitions

indicators.note: one item entering another goes inside it, so the writing tool sits within the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, i.e. big
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author signing up for major contests open to all.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf and tennis, an open is a tournament anyone qualified may enter, such as the US Open.

clue.text: Troublemaker tries, stupidly, to protect gutless rioter

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the jumbled letters enclose the other piece
doing something stupidly means getting it in a muddle, so the letters of tries are reordered
a gutless word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An agitator foolishly attempts to shield a cowardly rioter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges the word tries as STIER, and 'to protect' wraps it round the two outer letters of rioter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stirs things up deliberately causes trouble, so the word is a synonym for an agitator.

clue.text: Showing excellent vision, Tokyo won this Olympic bid

definitions.meaning: normal sharp eyesight is described with the numbers of the standard eye test, seeing at twenty feet what should be seen at twenty feet
Tokyo was awarded the Summer Games for the year written with those two numbers, held in 2021 after the pandemic delay

explanation.surface: Praising a successful Olympic bid as clear-sighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same number pair: perfect eyesight and the year of the Tokyo Olympics.

clue.text: One taking to a certain party, say booze

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so a sound-alike is entered

parts.words: One taking to a certain party
parts.note: someone who sides with a particular party in a dispute is a sider

explanation.surface: A partygoer bringing alcohol along to a do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks like a celebration but means a side in a dispute; one who sides is a SIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented apple juice is an alcoholic drink, so it counts as booze.

clue.text: Trailer parking right alongside edge of rifle range

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for parking on road signs

indicators.note: the edge of a word can be its end, here the last letter of rifle

parts.note: a view is the range of what can be seen

explanation.surface: A caravan parked beside a shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' suggests a caravan but means a film advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema trailer gives an advance look at a forthcoming film, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Start in earnest to embrace foreign food

indicators.note: the words embrace, or hold within them, a run of consecutive letters

explanation.surface: Advice to begin taking a dish from abroad seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartine is a French open sandwich, a slice of bread with a spread or topping.

clue.text: Warning: she may lead you astray

definitions.meaning: an alarm such as a police car's wailing device gives warning
in Greek myth these sea nymphs lured sailors to wreck with their singing; hence a seductive woman

explanation.surface: A caution against a tempting woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the wailing alarm and the alluring mythical temptress.

clue.text: Comeback from a Republican claiming "fake news"

indicators.note: claiming here means taking hold of, so the outer pair clasp the shuffled letters

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican in US politics

indicators.note: something fake is made up, so the letters of news are rearranged

explanation.surface: A US politician hits back with the familiar cry of fake news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' scrambles the word news, and 'claiming' sets that jumble between the A and the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A comeback is a retort or reply, which is a synonym for a response.

clue.text: Disreputable lawyer, retiring and mostly stern

parts.note: a retiring person is shy and reserved

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so stern loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Describing a lawyer of poor repute as introverted and severe.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Americanism for an unscrupulous professional, especially a crooked attorney.

clue.text: Paint Raymond keeps something for pending tasks

indicators.note: the words keep, or hold within them, a run of consecutive letters spanning both

explanation.surface: An artist named Raymond holding on to something.
explanation.definitionFit: An office tray holds incoming papers still awaiting attention, work not yet dealt with.

clue.text: Wandering around, detective wears no protective clothing

indicators.note: the detective is wearing the coat, so the clothing goes around him

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat that protects against the wet
DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police

explanation.surface: A roaming detective going about without a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads roam from place to place with no fixed home, so the adjective means roving.

clue.text: Mammal's lair covered with rubbish

indicators.note: the lair is covered over by the rubbish, so it sits inside it

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: An animal's burrow buried under litter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats, mice and squirrels are gnawing mammals of this order.

clue.text: Important final pieces of tape disguised how paintwork may be vandalised

parts.note: a key issue is a crucial or important one

indicators.note: the final pieces of the words are their last letters

explanation.surface: Vital masking tape ends being used to hide damage to paintwork.
explanation.walkthrough: To key a car is to scratch its paint with a key, a form of vandalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratching a car's finish with a key is a common act of vandalism, described by this verb.

clue.text: American friend turns up with excellent port

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: bud is American slang for a pal, short for buddy
A1 means first-class, written here as the letters A I

explanation.surface: An American pal arrives with a superb fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the wine but means a harbour city in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is a major Gulf city and shipping hub in the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Show Mal bizarre scientific theory

indicators.note: bizarre means weird or out of order, so the letters of show mal are mixed up

explanation.surface: An invitation to show a man called Mal something odd in science.
explanation.definitionFit: This physics principle says current through a conductor is proportional to voltage.

clue.text: Be, for the most part, extremely ill-disposed and very cross

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so live loses its last letter

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay mostly hostile and furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts LIVE (be, exist) to LIV; 'extremely' gives ID from ill-disposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone livid is furious, a stronger word for angry.

clue.text: Remarkable reason you can't book a restaurant?

definitions.text: reason you can't book a restaurant?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, ... means there is nowhere free to sit

explanation.surface: An extraordinary excuse for failing to get a restaurant reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth noting is striking, while split in two it means no seat is free to book.

clue.text: County name from French and German?

parts.note: de is the French word for from
von is the German word for from, the same word understood again

explanation.surface: Asking whether a county's name comes from two European languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' serves both languages: DE in French, VON in German.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a county in south-west England, part of the West Country, home to Exeter and Plymouth.

clue.text: MC: I dare say it represented the end of the war

indicators.note: re-presented, or presented anew, means the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies announcing an event for the end of a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleventh November marks the signing of the truce that ended the First World War.
